newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Opel Belgium sees 12 pct fall in output in 97.
newsitem.headline: Opel Belgium sees 12 pct fall in output in 97.

text.p: Opel Belgium, the Antwerp based assembly unit of U.S. car maker General Motors, said on Tuesday it would make 12 percent fewer cars in 1997 and expected to have to lay off a large section of staff temporarily.
"The planning is for total assembly of 300,000 cars in 1997," spokesman Dirk Snauwaert said. The quota is alloted by GM's GM Europe. It compares with 340,000 for 1996.
Actual production in 1996 would come out at about 300,000, he said, blaming the shortfall on the start-up of new production techniques in August and on a strike in April.

The cut in the 1997 quota reflected market conditions, especially a shift by consumers away from mid-range cars such as the Opel Astra and Vectra models assembled in Antwerp. Snauwaert said consumers' focus had swung towards small cars.

The reduction in output would affect some 6,600 of Opel Belgium's total 7,500 staff. The length of the temporary layoffs would be agreed in consultation with the works council at a meeting next week, Snauwaert said.
The contracts for temporary staff would also be extended by six months.
